details.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock affecting Val
Verde County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock.

* WHEN...Until early Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, (2.4 meters), Moderate lowland flooding
reaches the Highway 163 bridge floor several miles below Juno.
This level is turbulent and dangerous for inexperienced swimmers,
canoeists and kayakers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 1:15 PM CDT Sunday was 11.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 3.2 feet early
Friday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
8.2 feet on 08/31/2022.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive
cars through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning by 830 AM CDT.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Reno; Harvey; Butler; Kingman; Sedgwick; Harper; Sumner; Cowley

details.description:
* WHAT...For the Heat Advisory, heat index values around 105
expected. For the Extreme Heat Watch, dangerously hot conditions
with heat index values up to 110 possible.

* WHERE...Butler, Cowley, Harper, Harvey, Kingman, Reno, Sedgwick,
and Sumner Counties.

* WHEN...For the Heat Advisory, from 1 PM to 9 PM CDT Monday. For the
Extreme Heat Watch, from Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events. Hot temperatures and high
humidity may cause heat illnesses.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

details.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Babylon Burn Scar in...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

* At 110 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over western portions of the Babylon Burn Scar. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.


HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around western
portions of the Babylon Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
western portions of the Babylon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of Central San Juan County including western
portions of the Babylon Burn Scar
details.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and
ditches in the Babylon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1042 AM AKDT, moderate rain is falling in Seward and
vicinity causing water levels along local rivers and streams
to begin to rise. Rainfall will become heavy at times this
afternoon and continue through tonight before rain lightens
up on Monday. Total rainfall amounts through Monday afternoon
will range from 4 to 6 inches, with highest amounts in the
mountains. Rapid river rises will cause flooding along area
rivers, creeks, and streams and nearby roads. The Seward
Airport runway will also flood and could be covered with
debris from the Resurrection River.
- Water levels will crest Monday morning through Monday
afternoon, then quickly begin to fall Monday night through
Tuesday. Rainfall will taper off late Monday afternoon or
early Monday evening. There will be a brief break in the
rain, with the next round of light to moderate rain moving in
for Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday night.

details.instruction:

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive

suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
